nodes.title: Executable HRR acceptance test: rustls 0.23.46 server vs RUSTSEC-2026-0349-shaped ClientHellos (6/6 as expected)
nodes.summary: Hand-built TLS1.3 ClientHello probes against rustls =0.23.46 + aws-lc-rs =1.18.2 ServerConnection (2026-10-25). T1 default config, supported_groups [X25519MLKEM768, X25519], key_share only X25519 -> HelloRetryRequest selecting 0x11EC. T5 same with P-256 share -> HRR 0x11EC. T6 MLKEM share -> ServerHello 0x11EC. T2 default config, groups [X25519, X25519MLKEM768], X25519 share -> ServerHello X25519 (classical accepted: server follows CLIENT order). T3 'pq-required' config (CryptoProvider.kx_groups=[X25519MLKEM768]) same input -> HRR 0x11EC. T4 pq-required, client offers only X25519 -> alert 40 (NoKxGroupsInCommon). Full-handshake check: real rustls client with kx order [X25519, X25519MLKEM768] vs pq-required -> negotiated X25519MLKEM768, HandshakeKind FullWithHelloRetryRequest; vs default -> X25519, Full. Verdict for q2-002: YES, the rustls server sends HRR to X25519MLKEM768 when the client lists it FIRST but shares only X25519 (the exact RUSTSEC-2026-0349 shape), so the downgrade does not succeed against a default rustls server; it does NOT when the client lists X25519 first.
nodes.specifics: Code: state/raw/round-003/03-work/hrr_acceptance_test.rs (test module, invariants PQ-KX-1/PQ-KX-2) and state/raw/round-003/03-work/pqauth/src/main.rs (probe(), raw_client_hello()). Output: state/raw/round-003/03-work/run1.txt lines HRRTEST. Knobs: 0.23.x = only CryptoProvider.kx_groups (no group-preference knob; ignore_client_order affects cipher suites only, hs.rs:555-660 group = first client-listed group the server supports, tls13.rs:227 HRR if no share). main 28ee6c68 (2026-10-23): ServerConfig.kx_selector: &dyn KeyExchangeSelector, default PreferClientOrder, alternative PreferServerOrder (commit 3fe60d7913 2026-10-12; 483f623e3b 2026-10-13), OfferedKxGroup.has_key_share. CI gate: five verdicts frozen; any change blocks a rustls bump.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Probe ClientHello is minimal (no PSK, no ECH, no SNI-less cases); verdicts are for TLS-over-TCP rustls ServerConnection, QUIC path not probed (rustls#3229 QUIC+HRR fix present in 0.23.46 source). Hand-built X25519 share is a constant (server computes with it in T2 only).
nodes.underclaim_risk: The test passing does not make the default profile downgrade-proof: T2 shows a client that lists X25519 first gets classical, which RFC 9846 allows; the only server-side remedy on 0.23.x is removing classical groups.

numbers_checked.claim: server HRRs to 0x11EC when listed first without share
rustls servers not exploitable by key-share-prediction downgrade (crate-rustls-pq)
numbers_checked.source_value: true only if client lists hybrid first (T2 counterexample)

nodes.title: rustls server group selection = client order in 0.23.46; server-preference only via 0.24-dev KeyExchangeSelector
nodes.summary: Source-verified: rustls 0.23.46 ServerConfig picks the first group in the client's supported_groups that its provider supports, HRRs if the client sent no share for it; there is no server-preference knob for groups in 0.23.x. On main (0.24.0-dev.2, commit 28ee6c68 2026-10-23) a new KeyExchangeSelector trait (PreferClientOrder default, PreferServerOrder optional) lets a server prefer X25519MLKEM768 even when a client lists X25519 first, at the cost of one HRR round trip for such clients.
nodes.specifics: 0.23.46 src/server/hs.rs:555-660; src/server/tls13.rs:195-245; main rustls/src/server/config.rs:757-818 (PreferClientOrder/PreferServerOrder), :79 kx_selector field, :732 default &PreferClientOrder. PR #3370 (open 2026-10-19): client accepts ServerHello share for a component group it did not offer after HRR (client-side, hybrid component) - track.
nodes.overclaim_risk: PreferServerOrder is unreleased; API may change before 0.24.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Server-order PQ preference is one config line once 0.24 ships; reversal condition for the golden profile.

nodes.title: Pitfall (measured): rustls default-features=false without 'prefer-post-quantum' puts X25519 FIRST -> classical handshakes
nodes.summary: With rustls =0.23.46 and default-features=false, features [aws-lc-rs,std,tls12] (a common pattern in hyper-rustls/reqwest/tokio-rustls dependents), DEFAULT_KX_GROUPS becomes [X25519, SECP256R1, SECP384R1, X25519MLKEM768]; the client sends an X25519 share and lists X25519 first, and against a client-order server (rustls default) the handshake is classical. Observed in our first run: group=X25519, ClientHello 319 B instead of 1539 B. Enabling 'prefer-post-quantum' restores X25519MLKEM768 first.
nodes.specifics: Source: rustls-0.23.46/src/crypto/aws_lc_rs/mod.rs:254-262 (cfg(feature="prefer-post-quantum")). L5 CI gate: `cargo tree -e features -i rustls | grep prefer-post-quantum` must match for every rustls in the lock (server AND outbound clients: DB drivers, upstream proxies); plus a runtime assert that ClientConfig.crypto_provider().kx_groups[0].name()==X25519MLKEM768 (or MLKEM1024 in gov profile).
nodes.overclaim_risk: Only affects configs built from default_provider(); explicit kx_groups lists are unaffected.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Silent: no warning, handshake succeeds; HNDL exposure for outbound traffic of the golden if any dependency disables default features.

nodes.title: Measured ML-DSA-44/65/87 vs ECDSA/Ed25519 TLS 1.3 handshakes in rustls: bytes, TCP segments vs initcwnd 10, QUIC amplification, server/client CPU
nodes.summary: Own measurement 2026-10-25, rustls 0.23.46/aws-lc-rs 1.18.2, in-memory, X25519MLKEM768, server sends leaf+intermediate (rcgen 0.14.10 chains), no SCTs, no cert compression. Server first flight SH..Finished: ECDSA-P256 2,138 B (2 segments @MSS 1448); Ed25519 2,002 (2); ML-DSA-44 11,680 (9 segments: fits initcwnd 10 = 14,480 B with 2.8 KB headroom); ML-DSA-65 15,627 (11: exceeds initcwnd -> +1 RTT on a cold TCP path); ML-DSA-87 20,883 (15: +1 RTT); CNSA 2.0 profile (pure ML-KEM-1024 + ML-DSA-87) 21,331 (15). ClientHello 1,539 B (1,849 B with ML-KEM-1024). QUIC (modeled from exact CRYPTO bytes; 1200-B datagrams, ~50 B/packet overhead): client CH needs 2 Initials -> 3x budget = 6 datagrams; ECDSA needs 2 (OK), ML-DSA-44 11, ML-DSA-65 14, ML-DSA-87 19 -> every ML-DSA chain is anti-amplification-limited (extra RTT unless address already validated). Server CPU/handshake (median of 10x100, two independent runs): ECDSA 103.6/103.8 us; Ed25519 ~90; ML-DSA-44 194.3/197.2 (+88%); ML-DSA-65 255.8/266.0 (+150%); ML-DSA-87 282.9/276.3 (+170%); CNSA2 268.7/282.5. Client verify+kx: ECDSA 243, ML-DSA-44 177 (faster than ECDSA), ML-DSA-65 240, ML-DSA-87 303 us.
nodes.specifics: DER sizes leaf/intermediate/root: ECDSA 343/394/381; ML-DSA-44 3940/3989/3978; ML-DSA-65 5469/5518/5507; ML-DSA-87 7427/7476/7465; Ed25519 279/328/317. ML-DSA PKCS#8 = 54 B (seed form). Hardware: Intel i9-14900HX, 32 threads, host load average 36-77 (shared with sibling agents) -> CPU absolute values noisy, ratios stable across runs (within ~5%). Derived (E): a WebPKI-style ML-DSA-44 chain with 2 embedded ML-DSA-44 SCTs adds ~4.8 KB -> ~16.5 KB > initcwnd; leaf-only (intermediate elided via trust anchor IDs) ML-DSA-44 ~7.7 KB = 6 segments but still 7 QUIC datagrams vs 6 budget; MTC landmark-relative with ML-DSA-44 leaf key ~= 2.35 KB cert + 2.42 KB CV -> ~6.1 KB flight (5 segments, ~6 datagrams: at the QUIC budget edge).
nodes.overclaim_risk: In-memory: segment and QUIC datagram counts are computed from exact bytes with fixed MSS/overhead constants, not captured on a wire; CPU numbers under heavy host contention; no RFC 8879 compression (ML-DSA keys/signatures are essentially incompressible, but ASN.1 boilerplate is).
nodes.underclaim_risk: ML-DSA-44 private-PKI chains fit TCP initcwnd and verify FASTER than ECDSA on the client; for internal mTLS / origin pulls the cost is ~+90 us server CPU and ~+9.5 KB, which is affordable.

numbers_checked.claim: ML-DSA chain +~14.7 kB (pq-size-mtu-reality, Cloudflare WebPKI estimate incl 2 SCTs)
numbers_checked.source_value: +9,542 B measured for 2-cert chain without SCTs; +~14.3 KB with 2 SCTs derived

numbers_checked.claim: ML-DSA chain cannot fit QUIC 3x budget

nodes.title: Acceptance criterion: QUIC listener with PQ certificates must not exceed 2 RTT; use Retry/NEW_TOKEN-validated paths or keep ECDSA on QUIC
nodes.summary: From measured CRYPTO bytes: any ML-DSA chain (>=10.5 KB handshake-space bytes) exceeds the 3x anti-amplification budget of a 2-Initial ClientHello (~7.2 KB), so a cold QUIC handshake needs >=1 extra RTT. Rule for the golden: public QUIC listener serves ECDSA/Ed25519 (or future MTC) only; ML-DSA certs allowed on QUIC only for clients with a validated address (NEW_TOKEN) or on TCP.
nodes.specifics: Gate: harness counts server datagrams before first client Handshake ACK; assert <= 3 x client bytes and total handshake RTT <= 2 with ML-DSA-44 leaf+intermediate; record result per release.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Packet overhead constant approximated; coalescing changes counts by ~1 datagram.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Clients with larger Initials (Firefox 1350 B) raise the budget slightly; still insufficient for ML-DSA chains.

nodes.title: Header-size ceilings for 5-16 KB PQ-signed capability tokens (source lines, 2026-10-23..25)
nodes.summary: hyper 1.12.0 (golden pin) HTTP/2 server: DEFAULT_SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE 16 KiB (src/proto/h2/server.rs:40; RFC 7541 accounting name+value+32 per field) -> a 16 KB token header fails, ~15.9 KB is the ceiling minus all other headers; HTTP/1.1: DEFAULT_MAX_BUFFER_SIZE 8192+4096*100 = 417,792 B (proto/h1/io.rs:23), max 100 headers (role.rs:31) -> fits. h2 0.4.20 codec default 16 MiB (codec/framed_read.rs:22) but hyper overrides to 16 KiB. nginx master 9a7439fd (2026-10-23): client_header_buffer_size 1k, large_client_header_buffers 4 8k (src/http/ngx_http_core_module.c:3628-3632) -> any single header line >8 KB rejected (HTTP/1: 400 'Request Header Or Cookie Too Large'; HTTP/2 uses same directive since http2_max_header_size deprecation). Envoy main a0fd7327 (2026-10-25): max_request_headers_kb default 60 KiB, max 8192 (http_connection_manager.proto field 29) -> 431; max_headers_count 100; nghttp2 per-field ~100 KB. Node v26.12.1: --max-http-header-size default 16 KiB (since v13.13.0) and undici defaults its maxHeaderSize to http.maxHeaderSize (lib/dispatcher/client.js:65-69). Cloudflare edge: request headers 128 KB total, URL 16 KB (connection-limits page updated 2026-10-22).
nodes.specifics: Verdict per token size (single header, base64url): 5 KB: OK everywhere. 8-11 KB (3-hop ML-DSA-44 = 11.2 KB raw, ~15 KB b64): FAILS nginx default; OK Envoy, CF; borderline hyper h2 & Node (16 KiB total incl. all headers). 16 KB+: FAILS nginx, hyper h2 default, Node/undici default; OK Envoy (60 KiB) and Cloudflare (128 KB). Golden config: hyper http2 max_header_list_size = 65536 only on routes that accept Tier-X tokens; prefer body or by-reference handle; document nginx 'large_client_header_buffers 4 32k' for operators fronting us.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Cloudflare per-header limit not documented (only total); Workers/other CF products may differ; nginx HTTP/3 module limits not checked.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Header limits are a hard interop wall: a 16 KB token header silently fails behind default nginx or Node, independent of our server.

nodes.title: Multi-KB tokens are never HPACK/QPACK-indexed by default: full retransmission on every request
nodes.summary: RFC 9113 SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE initial 4,096 octets; RFC 7541 s4.4 adding an entry larger than the table empties the table; RFC 9204 QPACK max table capacity default 0. h2 0.4.20 encoder refuses to index any header with len*4 > max_size*3 (>3 KB at default) (src/hpack/table.rs:153). So a 5-16 KB PQ-signed capability token in a header costs its full size (Huffman barely compresses base64) on EVERY request on the connection, unlike a 300-B Ed25519 token.
nodes.specifics: Implication: per-request overhead ML-DSA-65 single-block token ~5.3 KB raw/~7.1 KB b64 x requests; 100 req/connection = ~0.7 MB vs ~30 KB for Ed25519. Supports the two-tier token (MAC chain locally, PQ signature only at trust-domain crossing) and a by-reference session-bound handle after first presentation.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Peers may advertise larger tables; clients may still Huffman-compress.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Bandwidth cost is per request, not per connection.

nodes.title: CA/B Forum SC-106 (ML-DSA in TLS server certs) closed without ballot 2026-10-21; moved to proposed NonBrowser WG
nodes.summary: cabforum/servercert PR #679 'SC-106: Enable Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQ) Key Pairs in TLS Server Certificates' (opened 2026-08-26) was closed by its proposer on 2026-10-21 without a discussion period: Chrome, Mozilla and Cloudflare agreed to drop the 7.1.3.2.3 restriction (ML-DSA CA signing classical keys, a downgrade-protection use) but disagree on 7.1.3.1.3 (classical CA cross-signing ML-DSA: Chrome forbids for CT/no-benefit reasons, Mozilla wants it). Proposer will re-propose in a ClientAuth/NonBrowser WG once chartered. Earlier PRs #662 (closed 2026-08-11) and #624 'Add MLDSA-87' (closed 2026-06-29). So, as of 2026-10-25, the Baseline Requirements do not permit ML-DSA in publicly-trusted TLS certificates, and the browser path is MTC-only.
nodes.overclaim_risk: A NonBrowser WG profile could still appear in 2027 for SDK/IoT relying parties.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Anyone planning public ML-DSA X.509 for browsers in 2026-27 is planning against a closed ballot.

nodes.title: Chrome Quantum-resistant Root Program: test root store in Chrome 152 (Canary), ML-DSA-44-only cosigners, MTC -07 (and -05, not -06); policy draft v0.3.0
nodes.summary: googlechrome.github.io/chromerootprogram cqrp/testing (updated 2026-10-16): flags verify-mtcs + test-root-store, Chrome 152+ (Canary), PKI Metadata Fastpush component; Chrome 152 expected to test standalone and landmark-relative MTCs; cosigner keys ML-DSA-44 only (OID 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.3.17, AlgorithmIdentifier bytes 300b0609608648016503040311); standalone certs need >=2 cosignatures (CA + mirroring); test validity 7-day or 47-day max. Draft policy v0.3.0 (2026-08-14; v0.1 05-14, v0.2 06-17): MTC-only, initial CA operators = CT log operators usable before 2026-02-01, ACME RFC 8555 mandatory with ARI (RFC 9773) and acme-profiles, quarterly ARI tests for >7-day certs, DCV reuse <=10 days, subscriber keys MAY be ML-DSA-44/65/87 (pure only, no HashML-DSA). FAQ: Phase 2 Q1 2027 public MTC bootstrapping; Phase 3 Q3 2027 CQRS launch with 'optional downgrade protections'; ML-DSA private PKI from Chrome 150 (chromestatus 5174590524489728).
nodes.overclaim_risk: Policy is a draft; dates are targets.
nodes.underclaim_risk: ACME+ARI mandatory and 7/47-day certs means the golden's ACME client is on the critical path of PQ auth, not the TLS library.

nodes.title: What a server must implement to serve MTCs (draft-07) and where rustls/OpenSSL/Go stand (2026-10-25)
nodes.summary: Per draft-ietf-plants-merkle-tree-certs-07 s8-9: the server (authenticating party) does NOT fetch landmarks; it holds several credentials (classical X.509 chain, standalone MTC, landmark-relative MTC) and selects per ClientHello using the TLS trust_anchors extension (draft-ietf-tls-trust-anchor-ids-06, 2026-09-30); it SHOULD NOT send a landmark-relative cert without an RP signal (trust_anchor_negotiation), prefers landmark-relative when usable, falls back to standalone or classical. ACME client must send Accept: application/pem-certificate-chain-with-properties, parse CertificatePropertyList (trust_anchor_id/groups/negotiation), and poll the 'acme-optional-alternate' link (HTTP 202 + Retry-After) for the landmark-relative cert without blocking deployment. Sizes: landmark-relative proof 736 B (23 hashes, hourly landmarks, 5.4M certs/h/CA); standalone proof 384 B + cosignatures; 1,024 B covers 2^32. Implementations: rustls issue #3079 open (2026-06-03, maintainer: 'definitely want'); rustls PR #3376 'Add TLS trust anchor IDs' open (2026-10-21, experimental codepoint 0xca34 as BoringSSL, TrustAnchorResolver) = step 1; rustls #3214 open: signature_algorithms_cert not exposed to ResolvesServerCert (blocks per-client ML-DSA vs classical chain choice). OpenSSL PR #33014 (open, 2026-09-27) MTC-07 + TAI-06 feature branch (AI review flagged MTC leaf path skipping auth-level check). Let's Encrypt boulder #9082 align -05->-07 (open), PR #9102 standalone MTC endpoint (open). Go: #82402 UPKI revocation proposal (2026-10-21).
nodes.specifics: L5 interface sketch: trait CredentialSelector { fn select(&self, hello: &ClientHelloView{sni, sig_algs, sig_algs_cert, trust_anchors}) -> Arc<CertifiedKey> } with credentials tagged {kind: X509|MtcStandalone|MtcLandmark, trust_anchor_id, requires_negotiation}; ACME module must support ARI + profiles + optional alternates. Reversal: adopt rustls TrustAnchorResolver when #3376 merges.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Draft could still change (-05 -> -07 already broke Chrome compatibility with -06).
nodes.underclaim_risk: Server-side MTC is mostly certificate selection + ACME plumbing, not new crypto; it is buildable in 2027 on rustls once TAI lands.

nodes.title: Composite ML-DSA: LAMPS draft-19 in RFC Ed Queue; TLS draft WG-adopted 2026-10-20; exact sizes
nodes.summary: draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-sigs-19 (2026-10-20, 234 pp, intended Proposed Standard) is in the RFC Editor queue (IANA RFC-Ed-Ack); composite KEM -23 likewise. draft-ietf-tls-composite-mldsa-00 (dated 2026-10-20, posted 10-23, Standards Track) adopted from draft-reddy-tls-composite-mldsa-12: 16 SignatureSchemes, codepoints TBD (e.g. mldsa44_ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256, mldsa44_ed25519_sha512, mldsa87_ecdsa_secp384r1_sha512). Max sizes (App. A, pk/sig bytes): MLDSA44-Ed25519 1344/2484; MLDSA44-ECDSA-P256 1377/2492*; MLDSA65-Ed25519 1984/3373; MLDSA65-ECDSA-P256 2017/3381*; MLDSA65-ECDSA-P384 2049/3413*; MLDSA87-ECDSA-P384 2689/4731*; MLDSA87-Ed448 2649/4741; MLDSA87-RSA4096-PSS 3118*/5139 (*=maximum). Signature = ML-DSA sig || traditional sig over M' = 'CompositeAlgorithmSignatures2025' || Label || len(ctx) || ctx || PH(M). rustls: no composite support; Go: pure ML-DSA chosen (golang #78888), x/crypto/ssh composite proposal #82315 (2026-10-18); OpenSSL PR #32886 (open).
nodes.specifics: Token Tier-X per-block (next_pk + sig) with MLDSA44-Ed25519 = 1344+2484 = 3,828 B (matches pqc-capability-token-design). A composite TLS chain adds only ~65-72 B per certificate over pure ML-DSA-44 (measured pure ML-DSA-44 flight 11,680 B -> ~12.0 KB derived).
nodes.overclaim_risk: TLS codepoints unassigned; no browser has committed to composite.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Composite is the conservative hedge for long-lived signatures (tokens, releases) where size is ~+64 B over pure ML-DSA.

nodes.title: Deployable PQ authentication today: Cloudflare-to-origin ML-DSA-44 (Custom Origin Trust Store + Authenticated Origin Pulls)
nodes.summary: Cloudflare docs (pqc-to-origin, updated 2026-08-03; overview updated 2026-07-03): origin may present an ML-DSA leaf (private CA uploaded to Custom Origin Trust Store, replacing public CAs), and Cloudflare can present an ML-DSA client cert via zone/per-hostname AOP; keys must be seed-only encoding; TLS 1.3 required; Cloudflare sends an X25519MLKEM768 share first and accepts HRR. Visitor-to-edge PQ auth 'still under development'. rustls 0.23.46 can serve and verify ML-DSA-44 (aws-lc-rs PqdsaKeyPair::from_pkcs8 accepts seed, expanded or both; to_pkcs8v1 emits 54-B seed form) -> the golden behind Cloudflare can have end-to-end PQ confidentiality AND PQ authentication on the origin hop now.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Vendor doc; parameter sets other than ML-DSA-44 not stated; not tested against a live zone here.
nodes.underclaim_risk: This is the one PQ-auth hop an operator controls end-to-end in 2026; skipping it because 'WebPKI is not ready' is an underclaim.

nodes.title: Contrarian: advertising ML-DSA in ClientHello breaks some TLS-inspecting middleboxes (Go 1.27, Palo Alto Prisma Access)
nodes.summary: golang/go #81199 (open, 2026-08-28): after Go 1.27 added MLDSA44/65/87 (0x0904-0x0906) to signature_algorithms and signature_algorithms_cert, TLS 1.3 connections through Palo Alto Prisma Access (PAN-OS 10.2.10-h37, GlobalProtect 6.2.8-982) get connection reset; bisected to the sigalg additions only; requested GODEBUG opt-out. #80573 (closed 2026-07-26 as tldr.fail dup): Go 1.27 ClientHello ~1,467 B stalls behind some proxies. rustls 0.23.44+ also advertises ML-DSA schemes by default in signature_algorithms (aws-lc-rs provider) -> the golden's OUTBOUND clients may hit the same class of middlebox; no rustls report found (search 2026-10-25).
nodes.specifics: L5: outbound client profiles expose a switch to drop ML-DSA from signature_algorithms (provider.signature_verification_algorithms filter) for enterprise-egress deployments; keep on by default; inbound server unaffected.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Single vendor/version report; rustls exposure inferred (E) not observed.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Middlebox ossification hit PQ KEM (tldr.fail) and now PQ sigalgs; size and codepoint novelty both break things.

nodes.title: CNSA 2.0 TLS profile (draft-becker-cnsa2-tls-profile-05, 2026-10-22): pure ML-KEM-1024 + ML-DSA-87 only; measured 21.3 KB server flight in rustls
nodes.summary: Individual draft -05 (13 pp): client MUST offer ML-KEM-1024 {0x0202} first, server MUST select it and MUST NOT accept others for a CNSA-compliant connection; ML-DSA-87 {0x0906} is the only signature (cert and CertificateVerify); X.509 certs mandatory; no hybrid. rustls 0.23.46 does it today with kx_groups=[MLKEM1024] and ML-DSA-87 certs: measured ClientHello 1,849 B, server flight 21,331 B (15 TCP segments: +1 RTT vs initcwnd 10), QUIC 19 datagrams vs 6 budget, server CPU ~270-283 us/handshake.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Individual draft, not NSA policy; FIPS validation of ML-DSA-87 in the specific aws-lc-fips build must be checked separately (calibration target owns FIPS pins).
nodes.underclaim_risk: Government profile is implementable with the same crate pins as the public profile; only provider config and certificates differ.

nodes.title: PQ-authentication posture for the golden (decision with dated reversal conditions)
nodes.summary: Alternatives enumerated: (A) ECDSA-P256 X.509 everywhere; (B) pure ML-DSA X.509 on public listener; (C) composite ML-DSA X.509; (D) MTC when available; (E) KEM-based auth (AuthKEM/KEMTLS); (F) dual chains selected per ClientHello. Decision: public TCP/QUIC listener = ECDSA-P256 (or Ed25519) WebPKI chain via ACME now (B is blocked: CA/B SC-106 closed 2026-10-21, Chrome CQRS MTC-only; also ML-DSA-65/87 chains exceed initcwnd and all ML-DSA chains exceed QUIC amplification budget). Key agreement = X25519MLKEM768 preferred, HRR-enforced (r3pq.hrr-acceptance-test). Private hops (origin pull from Cloudflare, internal mTLS, upstream/DB mTLS) = ML-DSA-44 X.509 from an operator CA now (rustls 0.23.46 serves/verifies by default; +~90 us server CPU, +9.5 KB, fits initcwnd). Gov profile = pure ML-KEM-1024 + ML-DSA-87 per CNSA2 TLS profile (accept the +1 RTT). (C) composite only for long-lived signatures (tokens/releases), not TLS, until rustls supports it. (E) rejected for TLS: AuthKEM -07 is individual and LAKE/EDHOC is where AuthKEM is moving. Cert layer built as CredentialSelector so (D)/(F) are config, not code.
nodes.specifics: Reversal conditions (check monthly): R1 Chrome ships MTC verification enabled by default in Stable for CQRS (target Q3 2027) AND rustls merges trust_anchors (PR #3376) + MTC (#3079) -> add MTC landmark+standalone credentials to public listener. R2 rustls 0.24 released with KeyExchangeSelector -> switch public profile to PreferServerOrder (forces PQ KX for every hybrid-capable client at +1 RTT for X25519-first clients). R3 a CA/B ballot permitting ML-DSA TLS certs passes AND a browser root program accepts them -> reconsider (F) dual chains (needs rustls #3214 signature_algorithms_cert exposure). R4 Let's Encrypt MTC production (2027 target) -> golden ACME client must support ARI + acme-profiles + optional alternates. R5 a practical attack on ML-DSA or implementation break -> composite for private hops. R6 CRQC timeline estimates move inside 2030 -> enable ML-DSA leaf in MTC immediately when available. Pre-registered: P(Chrome Stable verifies public MTCs by default by 2027-12-31) = 0.55; P(CA/B permits ML-DSA in publicly-trusted TLS server certs by 2027-12-31) = 0.2.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Assumes WebPKI timelines hold; ECDSA public auth is not PQ-secure (forgery needs a live CRQC, not HNDL, so the risk window is deferred not removed).
nodes.underclaim_risk: Waiting for MTC on the public listener is right, but private hops and the gov profile can be PQ-authenticated today with no new code.

nodes.summary: gh:apple/apple-root-program tree has no MTC/PQ document; latest commits 2026-10-16 (EOSC questions), 2026-08-01 (policy v2.0). The 'draft MTC policy due end of October 2026' (secondary report in rec60-mtc-plants-chrome-apple-le) is not yet published there.
